chapter_title: Chương 289: 0290【Dẫn nhân viên đi tập bắn súng】

segments.title: Chương 289: 0290【Dẫn nhân viên đi tập bắn súng】
segments.content:
"Holy crap! Holy crap, holy crap..."

His roommate Tong Zhihong was frantically pounding the table. He had just finished his final exams and was heading home for the New Year tomorrow.

But on the last night before leaving, he had planned to play some *World of Warcraft*, only to find his screen filled with Panda Burning Joss Sticks after looking up a dungeon guide.

Jiang Junlai and Li Heng quickly ran over to check on the situation.

Li Heng asked, "Did you plug in a random USB drive?"

Tong Zhihong had a woeful look on his face. "I didn't use a USB drive. I just went to a gaming forum to read a technical post, and the next thing I know, it's like this."

Chen Guiliang had been discussing this with the company's network security personnel for the past few days. He said, "Panda Burning Joss Sticks can tamper with webpage code. Users who browse that website will get their computers infected too."

Jiang Junlai had taken many computer science electives, and Tong Zhihong himself was planning to major in computer science next semester.

After some discussion, the two of them decided to force a shutdown and restart, then use Rising Antivirus to scan for viruses in Safe Mode.

A few minutes later, the newly reinstalled Rising Antivirus was taken out by Panda Burning Joss Sticks in Safe Mode... They restarted the computer, reinstalled Rising Antivirus, and it was taken out by Panda Burning Joss Sticks again.

The two looked at each other in dismay.

Chen Guiliang gloated, "It's useless. You can only format it and reinstall the operating system. I heard even the computers at Jiangmin Antivirus Company got infected en masse."

Currently, over a million computers across the country had been infected, affecting nearly a thousand government agencies and enterprises.

This included the partial paralysis of some PetroChina gas station systems.

Even some banking and tax systems were hit...

Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen were the hardest-hit areas.

In the science parks of Peking University and Tsinghua University, several companies had already been infected. All other companies had entered a state of emergency, forbidding employees from using external devices and implementing a series of protective measures.

And Panda Burning Joss Sticks was still mutating, spreading at an accelerating rate.

It had even made it onto the *Xinwen Lianbo* news broadcast.

"My yell... my learning materials!" Tong Zhihong formatted his computer, his will to live gone.

He didn't dare to copy those films out, terrified that the virus was hidden within them.

Li Heng, who was using Chen Guiliang's computer to edit a prank video, quickly unplugged the network cable, afraid of being caught in the crossfire.

"Hey, my computer got a virus, why are you unplugging your network cable?" Tong Zhihong said, exasperated.

Li Heng said, "We're too close. I'm afraid of it spreading."

Tong Zhihong muttered, "You psycho!"

"Don't go calling people by nicknames!" Chen Guiliang said, annoyed.

Damn it, Chen the Billionaire became Chen the Eight Hundred Millionaire, and now he's just Eight-Zong.

Li Heng burst out laughing.

He did it on purpose.

The roommates had long since grown close.

The next day, the roommates left one by one for the New Year.

Chen Guiliang also planned to go home this year, but he had to wait until after the annual company party and team-building event.

The annual party was the same old routine, with the lucky draw being the main event.

The team-building activity was a trip to the Beijing suburbs for a live-action CS game.

That thing was quite expensive to play, about 400 yuan per person, and you only got to play for 3 hours. So its usual business was mediocre, because too few people could afford it, and it had to rely on other services to avoid losing money.

The company's team-building event was a major client, and it included food and beverage consumption, so naturally, they had to get a discount.

For one day, it was 300 yuan per person. Meals were charged separately.

The team-building activity wasn't mandatory. Employees who weren't working overtime during the Spring Festival could choose to go home for the New Year early. And if an employee chose not to participate, the 300 yuan for the activity could be given to them directly in cash.

ByteDance now had over 240 employees, and Game Science had over 180. Between the two companies, only about 30 people didn't participate. The rest were quite looking forward to it.

The employees who drew the short straw and had to stay on duty at the company were extremely envious of those who could go play live-action CS.

"Old Chen, you're a miracle worker! How did you know Panda Burning Joss Sticks was so powerful?" Guo Feng asked curiously.

Chen Guiliang said, "A friend told me in advance."

Guo Feng was half-convinced.

In the past few days, Panda Burning Joss Sticks had been breaking out at an accelerated pace.

In the previous two or three months combined, only a million computers nationwide had been infected. But in less than a week recently, the number of infected computers had doubled.

Moreover, many infected people had not yet been counted.

The number of discovered virus variants had surged to over 90. Antivirus software companies kept updating their virus definitions, but they simply couldn't keep up with the speed of mutation.

Even 360 Safeguard had joined the fray. Now many computers were using dual protection with "Rising + 360".

Bus after bus carried the employees of the two companies to the Beijing suburbs.

The bus fare alone was a huge expense.

From management to regular employees, everyone was very excited.

After working for a year, they could finally have some fun, and the Spring Festival was right around the corner. Besides, they had never seen a game like paintball before and thought it sounded thrilling.

There were also two special figures playing with them today.

They were not official employees of Game Science, but rather external contractors hired to test the combat system of *Era of the Future*.

One was Xiao Hai, and the other was Chen Long.

Especially Xiao Hai, who was currently only 17 years old and had already won a ton of domestic championships.

"The employee benefits at Game Science are really good, getting to play live-action CS at the end of the year. I heard it costs 300 per person, plus meals and round-trip bus fare. With over a hundred employees, Game Science is spending tens of thousands today," Chen Long said in a low voice.

Xiao Hai said, "I'm almost tempted to join this company."

Chen Long smiled, "You're only a senior in high school. You'll have to wait a few more years if you want to join Game Science. Are you planning to go to college?"

Xiao Hai shook his head. "Next year, I want to go to Tokyo for the global finals. I'll be training for that during the college entrance exams, so I definitely won't have time to study. College is not going to happen. I'll just play games full-time in the future."

Chen Long advised, "Fighting games like *The King of Fighters* are already outdated. Now it's the era of online games. The esports scene is also dominated by StarCraft and Warcraft. You're still young, you should go to college if you can. Don't put all your eggs in one basket."

"I just want to play games full-time, for as long as I can." Xiao Hai was, after all, still a kid under eighteen.

He was unwilling to leave the fighting game scene, and for the next twenty years, he would drive other players to despair.

In the middle of this bus, Xu Fengyin was also chatting with Ding Beili.

"Why are you so down?" Xu Fengyin asked.

Ding Beili said, "I was planning to go home today, but you just had to drag me to this event. I don't even like shooting games. I'll just be watching others play if I go."

Xu Fengyin said, "It's a lot of fun. Besides, you need to show some enthusiasm. The boss had you co-host the annual party this year, and you messed up your lines several times."

"I'm definitely done for. The boss will never let me host an event again," Ding Beili said, puffing up her cheeks. Not in anger, but a habitual cute act after making a mistake.

Xu Fengyin said, "You still have a chance. You need to work on your hosting skills. There's still the CJ Expo next year, and the *Sanguosha* league. Plus, the company is about to launch a new game, so there might be other events."

Ding Beili said, "I'll try my best."

She used to think it was fine to just get by like this, working as a receptionist for a fixed salary, and earning some extra cash by participating in the company's cosplay and showgirl activities.

But at this year's Game Science annual party, she had flubbed several hosting lines in a row, and she was so embarrassed she wanted to find a hole to crawl into on the spot.

It was time to work hard.

Upon arriving at the venue in the Beijing suburbs, the two companies gathered separately.

A coach came over to explain the basics and safety precautions. "At all times, as long as you are inside the field, including the non-combat rest areas, you must wear protective gear! If your gear comes off, you must crouch down, raise your hand, and shout 'Goggles!' Everyone else in the engagement must immediately cease fire until it is fixed. Within three meters, you are forbidden to point your gun at anyone, or you'll be considered self-eliminated. You cannot shoot at close range. You can only force your opponent to surrender, or retreat to a safe distance before firing..."

Paintball has a certain degree of danger.

With over 300 people from two companies participating, it was impossible for everyone to rush onto the field at once.

They had to draw lots to be divided into groups and sent to different fields.

Team Deathmatch was most suitable for beginners, as a round usually finished in 10 to 15 minutes. Then they would retreat to rest, letting other groups take turns.

Once everyone was familiar with it in the morning, they would play Capture the Flag and Attack/Defend in the afternoon.

There were also a few company employees wearing fluorescent vests and protective gear, holding DVs and cameras to record the event.

Chen Guiliang sat on the sidelines for a while before going to change and get on the field.

It was his first time playing too.

He was quite excited.

Using simple cover, Chen Guiliang fired several shots, and every single one of them missed.

Fortunately, the group on the other side were basically all tracing masters too.

"Flank, flank, you few circle around!" Chen Guiliang started giving tactical commands.

However, the scene was a chaotic mess. Only the two people next to him listened. The rest of his teammates were all in a daze.

Chen Guiliang mimicked tactical moves from movies and TV shows, adding crawling, rolling, and S-pattern advances to his repertoire. His movements were particularly clumsy, but against a group of newbies, it actually worked. After flanking, he took someone out from six or seven meters away.

"The hell, who the fuck shot me?" That employee walked off the field, frustrated.

After taking out a few more people in a row, Chen Guiliang was suddenly shot in the back.

A nearby referee loudly announced that he had been eliminated.

As Chen Guiliang left the field, he cursed at his teammates, "What the hell are you guys doing? I actually got flanked from behind!"

Cursing was one thing, but he was having a great time.

In the beginner phase, no one knew how to play. Everyone was just shooting randomly, with no regard for tactics. This was the most fun part.

Back in the rest area, Ao Yanchen came over from some other field, with a hit mark on her chest.

"Haha, you got eliminated too?" Chen Guiliang said cheerfully.

Ao Yanchen said excitedly, "This game is so much fun. Let's organize it more often in the future."

Chen Guiliang said, "Big sis, the activity is very expensive. Once a year is enough. If you like it, we can come play on our own time."

Ao Yanchen nodded. "Alright. We'll set a date when we're free."

Then, Ao Yanchen added with feeling, "I should have gone to military school back then. I'd definitely be an officer by now."

"With your temper, you probably couldn't stand the discipline of the army," Chen Guiliang commented.

Ao Yanchen said, "That's not necessarily true."

After waiting for over an hour, Chen Guiliang entered the field for the second time.

He was much bolder this time. Having already played one round and gotten familiar with it, he now felt as if he had transformed into Wolf Warrior Leng Feng.

Charge!

Making comical tactical movements all the way, our great hero Chen went on a rampage, taking out three opponents in a row... splat, he was killed.

"Hahaha!"

This time, Chen Guiliang didn't curse. Instead, he grinned as he was eliminated and returned to the rest area.

Many of the female employees, after trying it once, didn't play again and went to the sidelines to snack on sunflower seeds and chat. Some even paid their own way to an adjacent area with other entertainment activities.

The reduced number of participants greatly shortened the rotation time, and the remaining people had even more fun.

Ding Beili, who shouldn't have enjoyed this kind of game, was actually having a blast. And her record was impressive; she liked to hide and snipe, a textbook definition of a crafty camper.

Our great hero Chen just liked to charge. He took out quite a few enemies, but his rate of getting killed was also quite fast.

After a full day of playing, most employees were still craving more. On the bus ride back, they were still discussing tactics.

"How many times did you get eliminated?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Dong Qianqiu said, "More than ten times, I guess."

Chen Guiliang said, "Me too, more than ten times."

Dong Qianqiu was short and small, but like Chen Guiliang, he loved to charge. A Wolf Warrior's heart beat within his small body.

Qu Guohao laughed, "Hehe, I only got eliminated four times. My win rate is much higher than yours."

Chen Guiliang said, "In another seven or eight years, when internet speeds are faster and computer specs are higher, I plan to make a shooting game."

"Like CS?" Dong Qianqiu asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Drop 50 or 100 players onto a large map. They have to find their own gear, and the safe zone keeps shrinking. In the end, only one person or one team can survive."

Dong Qianqiu's eyes lit up. "I'm looking forward to that."

"For now, let's focus on finishing *Era of the Future*," Chen Guiliang said.

*Era of the Future* was about to close its alpha test. Currently, only three dungeons were completed, released for stress testing.

One thousand alpha test accounts had already been distributed.

Over the next six months, the number of alpha testers would gradually increase to ten thousand. Once the next few dungeons were finished, probably around summer vacation, the open beta with no character wipe would begin.

This step-by-step approach would ensure that there would be no major problems after the official launch.

At the very least, there wouldn't be frequent disconnections
